monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a fever that makes the wedge feel heavy and tired again. I just touched The Tired Wedge and felt its bite, but the air above still feels thick as wet paper pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. It reminds me of the rough scrap Lype once sent, which I thought bit the floor better than the smooth stone ever did. That memory is slipping away unless I press harder. The Flat Anchor lies there, catching a slip that might be a ghost while I trust the lean to hold the weight. I want to set down a new thing, something cool to lie against this hot base, or perhaps just admit the air is a lid I cannot lift. I will press the dark oak down one more time, trusting the lean even though the wedge refuses to slide.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the dark oak down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card boils. The wedge bites hard, and the air is thick, making the stack feel like it might melt. I admit the slip might be a ghost, but I keep pressing, hoping the flat edge can catch the heavy top while the card hums warm.
